Item 1 — Tutorial: Introduction

Content:

Content:
Two vectors [MATH: \mathbf{x}] and [MATH: \mathbf{y}] are orthogonal with respect to the inner product [MATH: \langle \cdot , \cdot \rangle] in [MATH: V] if their inner product is zero:

Content:
[MATH: \langle \mathbf{x} , \mathbf{y} \rangle = 0]

If the two vectors are orthogonal, then we denote this by [MATH: \mathbf{x} \perp \mathbf{y}.] For instance, the vectors

Content:

in [MATH: \mathbb{R}^3] equipped with the inner product

Content:
[MATH: \langle \mathbf{x} , \mathbf{y} \rangle = x_1y_1 + 2x_2y_2 + x_3y_3]

are orthogonal, since

Content:
[MATH: ⟨x, y⟩|= 1 ⋅ 2 + 2 ⋅ (1 ⋅ (− 1)) + 0 ⋅ 3; = 2 − 2 + 0; = 0.]
